- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction by 1–3%.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to match sentiment-driven mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; lag correction: if sentiment changes direction within 3 days, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days.
- In high-sentiment periods (e.g., 2+ consecutive positive sentiment), model tends to overfit recent highs; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day high.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 3-day moving average of true values as baseline for correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate late-period prices (last 7–10 days); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for days 20–30 if sentiment is weak or neutral.
